title: Rhoform Part Data (D3) v0
description: One part record: the typed, provenance-carrying description of a single physical component that Rhoform's static tier checks against (requirement D3). A record is INPUT DATA, not a generated artifact — unlike the netlist IR it may carry retrieval timestamps, because provenance requires them; determinism is preserved by hashing the record into the design lockfile, not by forbidding wall-clock fields here. The record carries facts EXTRACTED FROM a datasheet plus a citation to it; it never embeds or redistributes the datasheet itself (D3: PDFs are fetch-on-demand absent a vendor redistribution agreement). SCHEMA STABILITY: version 0 is versioned but explicitly UNSTABLE — `stability` is pinned to "unstable" by this schema so no consumer can claim a stability guarantee that v1.0 does not make. Promotion to a third-party contract happens at 1.x against the criteria in open question 8-Q3. Extension points are restricted to properties matching ^x_ where explicitly allowed; every other object is closed so that a typo is an error rather than silently discarded data.

^x_.description: Reserved top-level extension point. Tools must ignore unknown x_* members. EXTENSION POINTS CANNOT CARRY A PAYLOAD: an x_ member must be a scalar of at most 1024 characters, never an object or array. Closing only Source was not enough - review showed a datasheet could simply be embedded one level up, at the record root or on a pin, and the no-redistribution guarantee would have been just as false.

schema_version.description: Integer part-data schema version. This schema describes version 0. Any change to the record shape bumps this integer; consumers must refuse records whose schema_version they do not know.

stability.description: Machine-visible stability marker, pinned to "unstable" for schema_version 0 (requirement D3: "versioned but explicitly unstable in v1.0"). This is a const rather than an enum on purpose: a record asserting "stable" at version 0 FAILS validation, so the v1.0 instability promise cannot be quietly overridden by a downstream producer. The value becomes settable when the 8-Q3 promotion criteria are met at 1.x.

part_id.description: Stable two-segment identity `<vendor-slug>/<part-slug>`, deliberately matching the two-segment DNS-label shape used by the Rhoform package-identity rules so part and package namespaces read alike. This is a SLUG, not the manufacturer part number: `mpn` carries the exact vendor string including characters (slash, comma, spaces) that are not permitted here. Unique within a part library; the design lockfile keys resolved picks by this value.

manufacturer.description: Manufacturer name as the manufacturer writes it, e.g. "Espressif Systems", "Diodes Incorporated".

mpn.description: Exact manufacturer part number as printed by the vendor, verbatim including suffixes and punctuation. Orderable variants (tape-and-reel codes and similar) belong here when they are what the BOM must state.

description.description: One-line human description of the part's function.

lifecycle.description: Vendor lifecycle status. "nrnd" is not-recommended-for-new-designs. "unknown" is an honest default and is distinct from omitting the field, which asserts nothing. Lifecycle is advisory: it informs sourcing lints, never the electrical checks.

package.description: Physical package and the CAD footprint it binds to.

pins.description: Every logical pin of the part, sorted bytewise-ascending by `name` (determinism: a part library must diff cleanly). A logical pin may map to several physical designators when they are internally common.

units.description: RESERVED multi-unit field set (requirement D3: "Reserved before freeze: multi-unit/shared-package fields"). Present only for parts whose package holds several independent functional units — a quad NAND, a dual op-amp. Each unit declares its pin membership; power pins shared by all units are listed in `shared_pins` instead. Reserving these fields at v0 rather than adding them at 1.x is what keeps the eventual multi-unit rollout a non-breaking change.

shared_pins.description: RESERVED (multi-unit). Names of pins shared by every unit — typically the supply and ground pins that a schematic tool assigns to a separate power unit. Each entry must match a `pins[].name`; a pin listed here must NOT also be claimed by an individual unit's `pins` membership.

parameters.description:
The part's own defining characteristic values — the quantities that make it THIS part rather than another in the same family: "resistance", "capacitance", "inductance", "forward_voltage", "temperature_coefficient". For a jellybean passive this is the substantive content of the record; for an integrated circuit it is usually absent, because an IC's behaviour lives in its pins and modes rather than in a single value.

Distinct from `ratings`, which bounds how the part may be USED, and from `pins[].characteristics`, which describes one terminal. The part resolver matches abstract constraints ("a 10k 1% 0402 resistor") against these values.

ratings.description: Part-level (not per-pin) absolute-maximum, recommended-operating, and thermal data.

modes.description: Supply-current-per-mode (requirement D3, consumed by the T10 current/power budget checker and by D2 load-equivalent simulation stubs). Each entry is one named operating mode with the current it draws on each supply pin under stated conditions. Sorted bytewise-ascending by `id`.

sources.description: The documents this record's facts were extracted from. Deliberately shaped to match the SourceRecord emitted by the Rhoform datasheet-knowledge pipeline, which is the upstream producer of these records: same two-level identity (byte hash locates, content hash means), same closed license vocabulary, same origin restriction. Sorted bytewise-ascending by `source_id`.

provenance.description:
Per-field provenance (requirement D3), expressed as a map from RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into THIS document to the provenance of the value at that location. Keying by pointer rather than wrapping every value in a {value, provenance} pair keeps the data readable and lets one entry cover a whole subtree.

RESOLUTION RULE (normative): the provenance applicable to a value is the entry whose pointer is the LONGEST prefix of that value's pointer. The empty pointer "" therefore covers the whole document and is the natural place for a record-wide default; a more specific pointer overrides it. A record SHOULD carry "" so that every field resolves to something; a consumer that finds no covering entry for a field it depends on must treat that field as unsourced rather than assuming the record default.

A pointer that does not resolve to an existing location in this document is a defect. JSON Schema cannot check that cross-reference, so the part-library linter does.

propertyNames.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. "" is the whole document; "/pins/0/capability" is one subtree.

license_class.description:
License basis under which this record's facts as a whole may be published.

PER-FIELD LICENSE CLASS IS DERIVED, NOT DUPLICATED. D3 asks for a license class per field. Every field already resolves to a source through `provenance` (longest-prefix pointer match), and every source carries its own `license_class`, so the class applying to any individual value is exactly:

    field pointer -> provenance entry -> source_id -> sources[].license_class

Storing it a second time on each field would let the two copies disagree, and a record whose per-field licence contradicts its cited source is worse than one that has to be looked up. The record-level value here is the CEILING for the whole record; linter check L10 rejects any record citing a source more restrictive than that ceiling, which is what makes the derivation safe to rely on.

notes.description: Free-text engineering notes: datasheet ambiguities, internal inconsistencies, values deliberately not recorded. Never load-bearing for a check — anything a checker consumes must be a typed field.

LicenseClass.description:
Closed license vocabulary, adopted verbatim from the Rhoform datasheet-knowledge pipeline so records cross the two systems without translation. "vendor-public": published by the vendor without access restriction. "vendor-agreement": obtained under an agreement permitting this use. "open-cc": openly licensed under a Creative Commons or equivalent grant.

The pipeline's vocabulary has a FOURTH member, "restricted-nda", which is deliberately absent here: that material is never ingested, and the pipeline raises rather than constructing a record for it. Omitting it from this enum makes the same red line unrepresentable in a part record instead of merely discouraged.
LicenseClass.$comment: Mirrors LicenseClass in the aed-part-data pipeline (sources.py) minus RESTRICTED_NDA, which is rejected at construction there.

Bound.description: One end of a measured range. Either an absolute number in the enclosing Measure's unit, or a bound expressed RELATIVE to another quantity — real datasheets specify logic thresholds that way ("VIH min = 0.75 x VDD", "VIH max = VDD + 0.3 V"), and flattening those to absolutes would silently pick a supply voltage the vendor did not.

oneOf.description: Absolute value, in the enclosing Measure's `unit`.

RelativeBound.description: A bound of the form `factor * reference + offset`, where `reference` names another quantity in the design (a supply pin or rail). Evaluated by the checker once the referenced quantity is known; until then it is a symbolic interval, which is exactly what interval-arithmetic checking needs.

reference.description: Name of the referenced quantity — normally a supply pin name on this part, e.g. "VDD33", or a rail name the design binds it to.

factor.description: Multiplier applied to the reference. Defaults to 1 when absent.

offset.description: Additive offset in the enclosing Measure's `unit`, applied after `factor`. Defaults to 0 when absent.

^x_.description: Reserved measure extension point. EXTENSION POINTS CANNOT CARRY A PAYLOAD: an x_ member must be a scalar of at most 1024 characters, never an object or array. Closing only Source was not enough - review showed a datasheet could simply be embedded one level up, at the record root or on a pin, and the no-redistribution guarantee would have been just as false.

Measure.description:
A datasheet quantity, carrying the statistics the vendor actually published and no others. At least one of min/typ/max/peak must be present: an empty measure is a defect, not an unconstrained value.

WHY `peak` IS SEPARATE FROM `max`: datasheets report these as different kinds of claim. `max` is a guaranteed limit the vendor stands behind; `peak` is an observed or characteristic maximum under stated conditions with no guarantee attached (Espressif's Wi-Fi current tables are 'Peak (mA)' columns; Diodes' 1 A dropout row has a typ and NO max at all). Recording a peak in the `max` slot would manufacture a guarantee the vendor never gave, and the T10 budget checker would then under-guardband. A checker that needs a hard bound and finds only `typ`/`peak` must either apply a declared guardband or report the budget as unverified.

unit.description: Unit symbol, UCUM-style with common SI prefixes ("V", "mA", "uA", "mV", "ohm", "Mohm", "degC", "mW", "pF", "ppm/K", "degC/W"). Dimensionless quantities use "1". Matches the unit vocabulary of the netlist IR's Quantity so values move between the two without reinterpretation.

peak.description: Observed or characteristic peak under `conditions`, explicitly NOT a guaranteed limit. See the note on this $def.

conditions.description: The test conditions under which these numbers hold. A measure without conditions asserts the enclosing context's conditions apply; a rating quoted outside its conditions is not usable, so conditions are recorded wherever the datasheet states them.

Conditions.description: Test/operating conditions, as a map from condition name to its value. Values are either a Measure (a numeric condition such as an ambient temperature or a load current) or a string (a categorical condition such as a drive-strength setting or a modulation mode). Deliberately an OPEN map: the condition vocabulary is part-family specific and is still being learned, and forcing it closed at v0 would push real conditions into free text where no checker can see them.

^x_.description: Reserved package extension point. EXTENSION POINTS CANNOT CARRY A PAYLOAD: an x_ member must be a scalar of at most 1024 characters, never an object or array. Closing only Source was not enough - review showed a datasheet could simply be embedded one level up, at the record root or on a pin, and the no-redistribution guarantee would have been just as false.

Package.description: Physical package identity and its CAD binding.

name.description: Package name as the vendor names it, e.g. "SOT223", "U-DFN3030-8", "0402", "ESP32-S3-WROOM-1".

pin_count.description: Total physical terminal count of the package, including thermal pads and shield terminals that are electrically connected. This is a property of the PACKAGE and may exceed the number of logical `pins` entries when several terminals are internally common.

footprint_ref.description: Library-qualified CAD footprint reference, `<library>:<footprint>`. Rhoform's own originally-authored library is `ael:`. Absent means the part has no footprint bound yet — legitimate for a D2 stub part, which can still be netlisted and type-checked.

thermal_pad.description: Whether the package has an exposed thermal pad. Affects the thermal path and therefore the junction-temperature check; recorded explicitly because its absence from a pin table does not mean the pad is absent.

PinRole.description: Electrical role, from the T2 pin-role lattice. This enum is IDENTICAL, member for member, to PinRole in the Rhoform netlist IR schema: part data supplies the roles that the IR carries and the ERC checks, so any divergence between the two lists would be a defect that only shows up at check time. Extending the lattice is a coordinated change to both schemas.

^x_.description: Reserved pin extension point. EXTENSION POINTS CANNOT CARRY A PAYLOAD: an x_ member must be a scalar of at most 1024 characters, never an object or array. Closing only Source was not enough - review showed a datasheet could simply be embedded one level up, at the record root or on a pin, and the no-redistribution guarantee would have been just as false.

Pin.description: One logical pin. FIELD-CLOSURE RATIONALE: the sub-objects a checker depends on (`abs_max`, `recommended`, `capability`) are closed and named, so a misspelling fails validation instead of silently disarming a check. Secondary electrical detail lives in the open `characteristics` map, where the vocabulary is still being learned and a closed list at v0 would push real data into free text.

name.description: Logical pin name as the datasheet names it, e.g. "VDD33", "OUT", "DISCH", "1A". Unique within the part.

numbers.description:
Physical terminal designators bound to this logical pin, e.g. ["1"], ["A3"], ["7", "EP"]. More than one entry means the terminals are internally common and the exporter may tie them.

ORDERING: natural sort - shorter designators first, then bytewise within a length. So ["2", "10"] and ["1", "40", "41"] are ordered, and plain bytewise would wrongly put "10" before "2". Stated precisely because the linter (L13) enforces exactly this rule, and a documented ordering that the checker interprets differently is worse than none.

description.description: Datasheet description of the pin's function.

unit.description: RESERVED (multi-unit): id of the `units[]` entry this pin belongs to. Absent on a multi-unit part means the pin is not part of any single unit — it must then appear in `shared_pins`.

abs_max.description: Absolute-maximum window for this pin: the stress limits beyond which damage is possible. Checked by interval containment (requirement T5); exceeding it is an error, never a warning.

recommended.description: Recommended operating window. Functional operation is only specified inside it; a design outside recommended-but-inside-abs-max is a warning, not damage.

capability.description: Per-pin current capability (requirement T10). This is the field D3 was required to reserve before freeze so the current/power budget checker has a source-side input.

characteristics.description: Open map of secondary electrical characteristics keyed by datasheet symbol, e.g. "vih", "vil", "voh", "vol", "leakage", "pull_up_resistance", "capacitance". Values are Measures, so conditions and relative bounds are preserved.

PinLimits.description: A voltage and/or current window for one pin. At least one of the two must be present.

voltage.description: Permitted voltage window at this pin, referenced to the part's ground unless `conditions` says otherwise.

current.description: Permitted current window at this pin. Sign convention: positive is current INTO the pin. A symmetric rating such as the 555's +/-225 mA is recorded as min = -225, max = 225.

PinCapability.description:
What this pin can DELIVER, as opposed to what it may be subjected to (`abs_max`) or what the part draws (`modes`). Requirement T10: sources declare capability, loads declare draw, and the budget checker sums draw per domain and checks containment against capability.

HONESTY REQUIREMENT: record the statistic the vendor published. A regulator whose datasheet guarantees `IOUT min 1.0 A` yields `source_current: {min: 1.0}` — a floor a checker may rely on. A microcontroller whose datasheet gives only `IOH typ 40 mA` yields `source_current: {typ: 40}` — no guaranteed floor at all, and a checker must treat it as such rather than promoting a typical to a limit.

source_current.description: Current this pin can source (deliver out of the pin).

sink_current.description: Current this pin can sink (accept into the pin).

^x_.description: Reserved unit extension point. EXTENSION POINTS CANNOT CARRY A PAYLOAD: an x_ member must be a scalar of at most 1024 characters, never an object or array. Closing only Source was not enough - review showed a datasheet could simply be embedded one level up, at the record root or on a pin, and the no-redistribution guarantee would have been just as false.

Unit.description: RESERVED (multi-unit): one independent functional unit inside a shared package.

id.description: Unit identifier, unique within the part, e.g. "1", "A", "gate1".

name.description: Human label for the unit, e.g. "NAND gate 1".

pins.description: Pin membership: names of the `pins[]` entries belonging to this unit. Must not include any pin listed in `shared_pins`.

swappability_class.description: Units carrying the SAME swappability class are functionally interchangeable, so a downstream pin/unit assignment step may permute them freely without changing the design's meaning. Units with no class, or with differing classes, must not be swapped. Named as a class rather than a boolean because packages exist whose units are only partly interchangeable.

Ratings.description: Part-level limits that are not attributable to a single pin.

thermal.description: Thermal resistances and characterization parameters, e.g. "theta_ja", "theta_jc_top", "psi_jt". Package-dependent: record the value for THIS record's package, and put the mounting/test conditions in the Measure's `conditions` — a theta_ja quoted without its board construction is not a usable number.

NamedMeasures.description: Open map from lower_snake_case parameter name to its Measure. Open for the same reason as `characteristics`: the parameter vocabulary is part-family specific and freezing it at v0 would lose real data.

^x_.description: Reserved mode extension point. EXTENSION POINTS CANNOT CARRY A PAYLOAD: an x_ member must be a scalar of at most 1024 characters, never an object or array. Closing only Source was not enough - review showed a datasheet could simply be embedded one level up, at the record root or on a pin, and the no-redistribution guarantee would have been just as false.

Mode.description: One named operating mode and the supply current it draws. The T10 checker sums `draw` per voltage domain; the D2 simulation stub turns each mode into a load-equivalent current sink.

id.description: Mode identifier, unique within the part, e.g. "wifi_tx_802_11b_1mbps", "deep_sleep_rtc_on".

description.description: What the part is doing in this mode, in the datasheet's own terms.

kind.description:
Coarse classification, so a checker can select modes without parsing ids. "active": doing work. "idle": powered and clocked but not working. "sleep": reduced-power retention state. "shutdown": disabled. "inrush": transient startup surge, NOT a steady state — a checker that sums inrush into a steady-state budget is wrong, and this member exists so it can tell the difference.

Note that peak-versus-typical is a property of the MEASURE (see Measure.peak), not of the mode: one mode can carry both a typical and a peak current.

conditions.description: Conditions under which this mode's currents were measured, e.g. supply voltage, ambient temperature, CPU frequency, duty cycle. Two datasheet rows differing only in a condition (clocks enabled vs disabled) are two entries here, not one averaged entry.

draw.description: Current drawn on each supply pin in this mode. Sorted bytewise-ascending by `pin`.

pin.description: Name of the supply pin this current flows into; must match a `pins[].name` whose role is power_in. JSON Schema cannot enforce that cross-reference, so the part-library linter does.

current.description: Current drawn on that pin. Use `peak` for an unguaranteed observed maximum and `max` only for a guaranteed limit.

Source.description:
A cited source document. CONTAINS NO DOCUMENT BYTES — only the locator, the hashes, and the license basis; datasheets are fetched on demand and never redistributed by Rhoform (requirement D3).

THIS IS THE ONE OBJECT IN THE SCHEMA WITH NO `^x_` EXTENSION POINT, and the omission is deliberate. Everywhere else `^x_` is an unconstrained escape hatch, which is what an extension point is for. Here it would have been a hole straight through the no-redistribution guarantee this $def claims to make: `x_pdf` could carry a base64 datasheet and still validate, so the guarantee would have been enforced by nobody. Review found exactly that, and found that negative control n10 was therefore proving less than it claimed. A closed property set with no escape hatch is what removes the SANCTIONED payload slot - the x_ namespace every tool is told to preserve. It does not, and no schema over free text can, stop someone base64-ing a PDF into a typed string field; every free-text field here carries a maxLength so the obvious attempts fail, but a determined producer can always abuse `mpn`. The guarantee this makes is narrow and worth stating exactly: there is no field here whose PURPOSE is to carry opaque data.

If a future source really needs an extra field, add it to this schema behind a version bump — which is the review a redistribution-adjacent field should get.

source_id.description: Identifier for this source, unique within the record and referenced by `provenance` entries.

vendor.description: Vendor slug that published the document, matching the datasheet-pipeline vendor registry where one exists.

url.description:
Canonical retrieval URL. HTTPS is required: an http:// citation cannot establish that the bytes hashed below are the bytes the vendor served.

Constrained by `pattern` rather than `format: "uri"` deliberately. In JSON Schema 2020-12 `format` is an ANNOTATION by default: Python jsonschema does not enforce it without an explicit format checker, and ajv rejects the schema outright in strict mode unless ajv-formats is loaded. A `format` here would therefore have looked like a constraint while enforcing nothing in either gate. Every keyword in this schema is one that both validators actually apply.

doc_title.description: Document title as printed on it.

document_version.description: Vendor's own version/revision designation, e.g. "v1.8", "DS37274 Rev. 5-2", "SLFS022K". This is the human-meaningful revision; `content_hash` is the machine-comparable one.

byte_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the exact retrieved bytes. A LOCATOR and cache key only: vendors re-serve the same document with new watermarks and timestamps, so this changes without the content changing. Required when `state` is "available".

content_hash.description: Versioned hash of the normalized extracted text — stamp-stripped, whitespace-collapsed, casefolded. This is the revision detector: byte_sha256 differing while content_hash matches is a harmless re-stamp, not a new revision. Only comparable between hashes minted under the same `identity_version`. Required when `state` is "available".

identity_version.description: Versions everything `content_hash` depends on: the normalization algorithm version and the vendor stamp-strip registry version, e.g. "chv1+reg2026.08.14". Hashes minted under different identity versions are NOT comparable. Format matches the datasheet pipeline's IdentityVersion string form.

retrieved_at.description: UTC timestamp of retrieval, RFC 3339 with a literal trailing Z. Timezone-aware and UTC-normalized so records from different machines compare directly. Enforced by `pattern` rather than `format: "date-time"` for the reason given on `url`, and deliberately narrower than RFC 3339: a non-UTC offset is rejected rather than silently normalized.

state.description: "available": the document was retrieved and hashed. "source-unreachable": every known URL pattern failed after a re-location pass. An unreachable source keeps its citation and its facts — vendors move PDFs constantly — but carries no hashes, which is why the hash fields are conditionally required rather than always required.

origin.description:
How the document was located. "vendor-direct": from the vendor's own site. "bootstrap-list": from a curated internal seed list.

Distributor-derived provenance is deliberately NOT a member. Distributor API results (MPN-to-URL lookups) are confined to a short-lived ephemeral cache upstream and must never reach a persistent record; omitting the value from this enum makes that red line unrepresentable here rather than merely forbidden by policy.

license_class.description: License basis for this specific document.

then.$comment: An available source must be byte-identifiable and dated; anything less is an uncheckable citation. content_hash is deliberately NOT required here: computing it means running the pipeline's text-normalization algorithm, and a hand-authored seed-library record legitimately has the bytes it downloaded without having run that pipeline. Requiring it would either block hand-authoring or invite producers to paste the byte hash into the content_hash slot, which would silently destroy the re-stamp-versus-revision distinction the two-level identity exists for. When content_hash IS present it must be accompanied by the identity_version it was minted under, since hashes from different versions are not comparable — that pairing is enforced by dependentRequired above.

Sha256.description: Algorithm-prefixed lowercase hex SHA-256, matching the hash spelling used by the Rhoform netlist IR (design_hash, source_hash) so hashes are recognizable across Rhoform artifacts. NOTE for pipeline integration: the datasheet pipeline emits bare hexdigests; the writer that turns pipeline SourceRecords into part records adds the `sha256:` prefix.

^x_.description: Reserved provenance extension point. EXTENSION POINTS CANNOT CARRY A PAYLOAD: an x_ member must be a scalar of at most 1024 characters, never an object or array. Closing only Source was not enough - review showed a datasheet could simply be embedded one level up, at the record root or on a pin, and the no-redistribution guarantee would have been just as false.

Provenance.description: Where one value (or subtree) came from and how much weight it carries.

source_id.description: Must match a `sources[].source_id` in this record.

locator.description: Where inside the source the value is found, in the document's own terms: "Table 6-3", "Section 5.5, Electrical Characteristics", "page 4". Human-checkable by design — a reviewer must be able to open the cited document and land on the number.

target.description:
Echo of the identity (`id`, `name`, or `source_id`) of the array element this entry's pointer resolves to. Required in practice whenever the pointer addresses an element of `pins`, `modes`, or `sources`.

WHY THIS EXISTS: provenance keys are JSON Pointers, which address array elements BY INDEX, while this schema requires those same arrays to be sorted by their identity field. Those two requirements interact badly — renaming one mode re-sorts the array and silently re-points every index-based provenance entry at a DIFFERENT element. The pointer still resolves, so an unresolvable-pointer check cannot catch it, and the record ends up confidently citing the wrong datasheet table. Echoing the intended identity here makes that failure detectable: the part-library linter compares this value against the element the pointer actually resolves to and rejects a mismatch.

confidence.description:
How the value relates to its source, ordered from strongest to weakest.

"datasheet-stated": appears verbatim in the cited document.
"datasheet-derived": computed from stated values by a documented rule (record the rule in `note`).
"vendor-confirmed": obtained from vendor support or errata rather than the datasheet body.
"estimated": an engineering estimate that is NOT in the source — guardbands and assumptions live here, and marking one "datasheet-stated" would launder an assumption into a vendor guarantee.
"unverified": imported without checking.

This field is ordinal on purpose and there is no numeric score: a 0-to-1 confidence invites false precision that nobody can calibrate.

method.description: How the value was captured. Separate from `confidence` because they are independent: an automated extraction of a stated table value is high-confidence, and a hand-entered guess is not.

note.description: Justification, required in practice for "datasheet-derived" (state the rule) and "estimated" (state the assumption and why it is conservative).
